rule.title: DNS TXT Answer with Possible Execution Strings
rule.author: Markus Neis

es.summary: Una respuesta DNS de tipo TXT contiene cadenas asociadas a ejecución de comandos (IEX, Invoke-Expression o cmd.exe). Esto puede indicar que un endpoint recibe comandos o payloads a través de DNS.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos DNS con record_type igual a TXT cuyo campo answer contiene, sin distinguir mayúsculas, 'IEX', 'Invoke-Expression' o 'cmd.exe'. Es el patrón de backdoors como DNS_TXT_Pwnage.ps1 de Nishang, que leen registros TXT y ejecutan su contenido.
es.why_it_matters: Los registros TXT permiten entregar comandos o scripts que atraviesan proxies y firewalls que solo inspeccionan HTTP. Corresponde a ATT&CK T1071.004 (protocolo de capa de aplicación: DNS) para comando y control, y suele preceder a la ejecución de PowerShell en el endpoint.
triage_steps: Revise el campo answer completo y el nombre consultado (query): identifique si contiene un comando, un script codificado o solo una coincidencia casual en texto base64.
Identifique el cliente que hizo la consulta (IP de origen, hostname) y si pasó por el resolvedor interno o salió directamente a Internet.
Investigue el dominio consultado: antigüedad, registrador, servidores NS, reputación y si otros hosts de la organización lo consultan.
Busque en el mismo host, +/- 15 minutos, procesos powershell.exe o cmd.exe con CommandLine que contenga IEX, Invoke-Expression, Resolve-DnsName o nslookup -q=txt.
Revise el proceso padre de cualquier PowerShell encontrado y el usuario que lo ejecutó; compare con su actividad habitual.
Pivote por el mismo dominio y subdominios: muchas consultas TXT con subdominios variables sugieren tunelización o C2 activo.
Consulte alertas previas para el mismo host, usuario y dominio, incluidas descargas o persistencia recientes.
false_positives: Claves DKIM u otros valores base64 en TXT que contienen 'iex' por azar, ya que la coincidencia no distingue mayúsculas.
Ejercicios de red team o pruebas de seguridad autorizadas que usan C2 por DNS.
Investigadores o herramientas de threat intel que resuelven dominios maliciosos conocidos para análisis.
Scripts administrativos internos que distribuyen configuración o comandos mediante registros TXT.
response_steps: Verifique con el contenido del answer y la telemetría del endpoint si hubo ejecución real del comando recibido.
Si se confirma, aísle el endpoint y bloquee el dominio en el resolvedor interno, el DNS sinkhole y el firewall.
Recolecte evidencia: memoria, historial de PowerShell, Script Block Logging y tareas programadas o claves Run creadas.
Elimine la persistencia y el script que consulta TXT; restablezca credenciales del usuario afectado.
Busque el mismo dominio y patrón en toda la flota y restrinja el DNS saliente directo hacia Internet.
es.severity_rationale: Nivel alto porque un TXT con cadenas de ejecución tiene pocos usos legítimos y señala un posible canal de C2 activo hacia un endpoint.

en.summary: A DNS TXT answer contains strings tied to command execution (IEX, Invoke-Expression or cmd.exe). An endpoint may be receiving commands or payloads over DNS.
en.what_it_detects: DNS events with record_type TXT whose answer field contains, case-insensitively, 'IEX', 'Invoke-Expression' or 'cmd.exe'. This matches backdoors such as Nishang's DNS_TXT_Pwnage.ps1, which read TXT records and execute their content.
en.why_it_matters: TXT records can deliver commands or scripts that bypass proxies and firewalls inspecting only HTTP. This is ATT&CK T1071.004 (Application Layer Protocol: DNS) for command and control, often followed by PowerShell execution on the endpoint.
triage_steps: Read the full answer and the queried name (query): decide whether it holds a command, an encoded script or an incidental match inside base64 text.
Identify the querying client (source IP, hostname) and whether the query went through the internal resolver or directly to the Internet.
Research the queried domain: age, registrar, NS servers, reputation and whether other internal hosts query it.
On the same host, +/- 15 minutes, look for powershell.exe or cmd.exe with CommandLine containing IEX, Invoke-Expression, Resolve-DnsName or nslookup -q=txt.
Check the parent process and user of any PowerShell found; compare with their normal activity.
Pivot on the domain and its subdomains: many TXT queries with changing subdomains suggest tunneling or active C2.
Review earlier alerts for the same host, user and domain, including recent downloads or persistence.
false_positives: DKIM keys or other base64 TXT values containing 'iex' by chance, since matching is case-insensitive.
Authorized red team exercises or security tests using DNS C2.
Researchers or threat intel tooling resolving known malicious domains for analysis.
Internal admin scripts that distribute configuration or commands through TXT records.
response_steps: Verify from the answer content and endpoint telemetry whether the received command actually ran.
If confirmed, isolate the endpoint and block the domain at the internal resolver, DNS sinkhole and firewall.
Collect evidence: memory, PowerShell history, Script Block Logging, and any scheduled tasks or Run keys created.
Remove persistence and the TXT-polling script; reset the affected user's credentials.
Hunt for the same domain and pattern fleet-wide and restrict direct outbound DNS to the Internet.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because a TXT answer with execution strings has few legitimate uses and points to a possible active C2 channel to an endpoint.

positive.description: TXT answer carrying a PowerShell IEX download cradle, as used by DNS TXT backdoors
TXT answer containing a cmd.exe command line

negative.description: Ordinary SPF TXT record with no execution strings
A record lookup for a host whose name mentions cmd but is not a TXT answer
